Ligand 2 is my best molecule but ligand 1 is the working one, so I will convert ligand 1 onto the same winning pattern by a different route, which also gives me a distinct molecule rather than a duplicate. Ligand 1 has the anilide NH already; what it lacks is the aryl-N(H)-azine link, and what it carries instead is a pyrazolyl biaryl at the para position - a motif I have now measured twice at only 0.03-0.05 once the sulfonamide is removed, so it is not pulling its weight. Step 1: atom 13 is the aromatic carbon bearing the pyrazole at atom 14 over a non-ring biaryl bond, so cut it and attach an N-linked pyridin-2-ylamino, the strongest link I have found.

Now remove the methanesulfonyl azetidine, which is 136 Da of saturated sulfonamide holding SA at 2.27 and TPSA at 95 while contributing no NH-azine link. Atom 7 is the exocyclic amide carbonyl and the 7-6 bond to the azetidine ring carbon is non-ring. I will attach a cyclopropyl rather than a methyl: a plain methyl would reproduce the acetanilide I have already made, whereas cyclopropanecarboxamide is a distinct, equally cheap acyl cap that keeps molecular weight at ~253 - nearer the band QED rewards than 227 - with LogP around 2.6 and only 2 rotatable bonds.
